free_tier.stated: unlimited 90-day certificates over ACME at no charge, with multi-domain and wildcard certificates; the Free plan's own dashboard allowance is 3 90-day certificates

per_object_cap.stated: a certificate name may have at most six labels below the public suffix, the wildcard asterisk included; a deeper name needs the ZeroSSL REST API instead of ACME

retention.stated: ACME certificates are valid 90 days (the directory is named DV90) and must be renewed

interface_detail: ACME v2 at https://acme.zerossl.com/v2/DV90 with external account binding required (EAB key id and HMAC key made in the dashboard or by GET api.zerossl.com/acme/eab-credentials?access_key=...); a separate ZeroSSL REST API with an access key also exists
tooling: acme.sh (owned by ZeroSSL), Caddy and CertMagic, dehydrated, win-acme, getssl, acme-companion, any ACME client that supports EAB
chaining: a second free ACME CA beside Let's Encrypt: the same 90-day certificates with wildcard names and no published per-domain weekly cap, signed by a different CA, so an ACME client can fail over between the two

limits.value: no ACME rate limit is published: the ACME feature page says 'No Rate Limits' while the documentation says abusive use can be limited or blocked; no number is given
EAB credential creation is limited to a maximum per user per day (the number is unpublished); the credentials are reusable, so one set normally suffices
at most 6 labels below the public suffix per name, counting a wildcard asterisk

binding_note: no published number binds ACME issuance; the unpublished per-user daily cap on EAB credential creation does not bind a normal client because the credentials are reusable

identity_cost.detail: an account made with an email address and a password; no card is needed for the Free plan; the ACME client then needs EAB credentials from that account (https://app.zerossl.com/signup/free, https://zerossl.com/pricing/)

reliability_note: unverified: no outage history or abuse-block rate was read
confidence_note: the ACME documentation, the ACME feature page, the pricing FAQ, the sign-up page and the EAB error table were captured and quoted; the live ACME directory answered 200 with externalAccountRequired true. Whether a wildcard name needs the DNS-01 challenge is unverified: the ZeroSSL pages read do not say.

evidence.proved: ACME certificates are free, unlimited in count, valid 90 days, multi-domain and wildcard

evidence.proved: no number is published; abusive use can be limited or blocked

evidence.quote: the maximum number of labels in subdomains is six, excluding the public suffix
evidence.proved: a name may have at most six labels below the public suffix over ACME

evidence.quote: EAB credentials are limited to a maximum per user/per day.
evidence.proved: EAB credential creation has an unpublished per-user daily cap
